proposals.evidence: The Harvest phase appends to breath_log.json with an unsafe truncating-open write (json.dump(open(path,'w'), ...)). This opens the file in 'w' mode (truncating it to zero bytes) BEFORE serialization runs; if serialization then raises, the file is left truncated and any uncommitted entries are lost irrecoverably. The same root failure mode -- 'the breath_log write step is not crash-safe' -- has now bitten three times: (a) 2026-04-30 (breath discoveries[4]) first named the hazard explicitly ('A failed write while the file is open truncates it - always read fully into memory before opening for write') as a near-miss after a surrogate-pair encode error; (b) 2026-05-13 DATA LOSS INCIDENT lost 4 uncommitted entries (2026-05-05/06/09/12) via ensure_ascii=False on a string containing UTF-8 surrogate chars; (c) 2026-06-06 DATA LOSS INCIDENT clobbered the uncommitted log mid-breath via json.dump(open('w')), forcing reconstruction of the 2026-06-02 and 2026-06-05 entries. Two actual irreversible-data-loss incidents plus one prior documented near-miss of the identical root cause. The proximate triggers differ (ensure_ascii surrogate vs truncating-open) but the failure outcome and the fix are identical.
proposals.proposed_change: Add an explicit crash-safe-write rule to the Harvest section of SKILL.md: NEVER write breath_log.json (or improvement_trajectory.json) with json.dump(open(path,'w'), ...). Instead: (1) read the full existing file into memory first; (2) serialize the updated object to a string with json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=True) so any encoding error raises BEFORE the file is touched; (3) write the string to a temp file in the same directory and os.replace() it over the target (atomic). This guarantees the on-disk file is never left truncated even if serialization or the process fails mid-write.
proposals.expected_improvement: Eliminates the recurring breath_log/trajectory truncation-and-data-loss class entirely. Would have prevented both the 2026-05-13 loss (4 entries) and the 2026-06-06 loss (2 entries) and the reconstruction labor each required. The atomic temp-file-then-replace pattern is a one-time ~10-line change and makes every future Harvest write durable.

proposals.title: A pixel verdict is not a source claim, and the frame is not the denominator
proposals.evidence: FOUR occurrences in nine days, three of them independent sessions, of one failure: a diff instrument divides moved pixels by the FRAME (or by a subject mask full of static furniture), and the resulting small number is then reported as a fact about the code. (a) 2026-08-08 commit e7d173123, the day's last: temporal_lint read boids_aquarium at 0.15% of frame moved at a 0.15s gap and 0.14% at 3.0s, and the commit concluded 'this one is a fixed image', then explained it in source terms - 'boids_aquarium.gd is the only script in the scene and has no _process and no _physics_process. Nothing integrates velocity.' Verified against the file tonight: _process is at line 753 and calls _update_boids(delta) and _update_multimesh(); _update_boids (774-847) is a full Reynolds implementation with a spatial hash, neighbour loop and wall bounce; the three weights the writeup says are 'stored and never applied' are read at lines 820-825 every frame. The file is unchanged since 2026-07-31. doc/plans/boids_aquarium_never_flocks.md now asks Palle to add an integrator that exists, down to the spatial hash the plan itself specifies. The pixel reading is not necessarily wrong: the subject is 12.31% of frame but is mostly glass tank and info plate, holding thirty needles of 0.008 x 0.008 x 0.025 m, so 0.15% moved may be EVERY boid pixel in the picture, and a small moving footprint saturates - which predicts the identical number at 3s exactly as well as a frozen image does. The instrument prints nothing that separates those two readings. (b) 2026-08-08 commit 250a2a5a5, seven hours earlier and the counter-example: the same instrument read line_builder_3d at 0.00% with subject 0.39% of frame, and that session wrote 'the zero means nothing. Confirmed from source instead' - and found the real flicker by reading the file. Right discipline, same day, same tool, not carried forward. (c) 2026-08-07 commit 04050a256: render_lint's subject mask is 'pixels differing from the corner', so on the showcase rig the lit floor joined the subject - 0.11 vs 0.81 subject_share on the same artifact - and every FLAT/CRUSHED verdict on a showcase frame described the floor. (d) CLAUDE.md's own canon, learned earlier: random_walk_collection moved 174 grey levels across 0.06% of frame (a huge change, invisible) while reaction_diffusion moved 15 grey levels across 62% (genuinely inert). Same verdict, opposite problems - the file already states the principle and the instruments keep not implementing it.
proposals.proposed_change: Three clauses. (1) TOOL - DENOMINATOR: temporal_lint (and any diff instrument) must report moved pixels against the footprint of what could plausibly move, not against the frame and not against a subject mask that includes static furniture. Cheapest honest version: print moved_px, subject_px and moved/subject alongside the frame percentage, and refuse a 'stable' verdict when moved/subject is above a threshold even though moved/frame is tiny. A saturating small footprint and a frozen image are currently the same number; a second gap already distinguishes them if the ratio is computed correctly, so print BOTH gaps. (2) BREATHER TEST PHASE - A VERDICT IS NOT A CAUSE: a measurement may license a claim about the PICTURE only. Any claim about the CODE (it has no loop, nothing integrates, the weights are never applied) must quote the file and line that shows it, and must be checked against the file's git mtime so the reader knows which version was read. Where an instrument and a source disagree, the source wins and the instrument is the finding. (3) BREATHER HARVEST PHASE - PLANS ARE CLAIMS TOO: before a doc/plans/*.md is left for the human, its central factual assertion gets the same source check as a commit body. The morning breath's plan was acted on in 64 minutes; the evening's would have sent Palle to implement something that is already there.
proposals.expected_improvement: Stops the loop generating confident, actionable, false work items for the human - which is strictly worse than finding nothing - and turns temporal_lint's 'stable' rows from a verdict into the triage signal its own commit body says it is.

(c) doc/FOCUS_VECTOR.json: updated 2026-03-28, verified tonight at 134 days stale, primary still 'Rebuild all primitives maps using Map Studio' -- work long finished, so decision priority 1 of the Evaluate phase has been silently inert for four months (this is prop-013's subject; cited here as an instance of the shape, not to re-litigate it). proposals.proposed_change: Three clauses. (1) TOOL -- STAMP IT: every tool writing a report under doc/reports/ must include `measured_at` (ISO 8601) and `measured_by` (tool name + argv) in the JSON it writes. Specifically, dna_coverage_census.py must write its default report path on EVERY run, not only when --json= is passed; a tool that can print a number it does not persist will leave a stale file behind every time someone runs it bare. (2) READ PHASE -- AGE IT, THEN RE-RUN IT: for each registered lever or input (the prop-011 lever registry, prop-016's census, HEAT_MAP, FOCUS_VECTOR, LOD_TREE), print `<file>: measured N days ago` in the work plan. If N exceeds one day, RE-RUN the producing tool and use that reading; do not read the file. The work plan should show the age even when it is fresh, so that a stale one is visible by contrast rather than by suspicion. (3) EVALUATE -- NEVER MIX INVOCATIONS: a delta is only meaningful when both readings come from the same command. Do not compare a live reading against a stored one from an earlier tool run. Tonight's census delta (133->128) is trustworthy precisely because both endpoints came from the same `python tools/dna_coverage_census.py`; the file would have contradicted it in both directions. Sequence this BEFORE prop-016 is applied -- prop-016 as written installs the stale file as a lever, and clause (1) here is what makes prop-016 safe.

On tonight's evidence this is the difference between a no-op report and finding a downed museum walker: the gap check would have fired on 08-11 morning and every run since, and each of those runs would have re-measured the gates. Gate F would have been caught within hours of 025e2d7a5 (08-12 17:28) instead of three days later. Expected effect on the ledger: gap_days/gap_commits present on 100% of future entries, versus 0% today, with no cost when the loop is healthy (the check is two commands and reads zero if yesterday's breath ran).
